incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: P1 — GPU allocation failed on cluster-prod-gpu-2. Error: CUDA out of memory (failed to allocate 536870912 bytes).

pagerduty: Paging tyler.h (primary oncall) — escalation level 1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

tyler.h: acked — looking now. any obvious customer-facing endpoints?

jess: I see spike in model-serving pods for model: /models/large-chat-v1 on namespace prod-serving. Replica 2 on node gpu-2 OOM loop.
	maria: telemetry shows ~150 qps to that model in the last 5m, tail latency spiked 2x. could be sudden traffic or batch size regression.

tyler.h: starting triage: kubectl -n prod-serving get pods -o wide | grep large-chat-v1

incident-bot: Command result:
```
large-chat-v1-2   CrashLoopBackOff   3/3   10m   10.0.0.42   gpu-node-2
large-chat-v1-3   Running            3/3   7m    10.0.0.43   gpu-node-3
```

jess: pulling logs from the crashing pod: kubectl -n prod-serving logs large-chat-v1-2 -c runtime --tail=200

incident-bot: Logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-14T03:12:08Z ERROR runtime: CUDA out of memory while allocating 512MB for KV cache
2026-03-14T03:12:08Z INFO  runtime: attempting retry with forced empty cache
2026-03-14T03:12:09Z FATAL runtime: GPU allocation failed, exiting
```

maria: nvidia-smi from node shows memory saturation on gpu0: 31.9GB used / 32GB. Processes: model runtime PIDs at high memory.

infra-bot: Detected possible memory leak pattern: model runtime increased memory steadily over last 30m on those pods.

tyler.h: immediate mitigations: 1) disable batching on that model instance, 2) shift traffic to large-chat-v1-3 (node-3), 3) scale up fallback smaller model if needed. I'll patch route and scale replica.

jess: walk-through commands:
```
kubectl -n prod-serving scale deployment/large-chat-v1 --replicas=4
kubectl -n prod-serving annotate svc/large-chat-v1 traffic-override='{ "exclude": ["gpu-node-2"] }'
```

pagerduty: User tyler.h acknowledged at 03:12:35 and is actively investigating.

tyler.h: scaled to 4 replicas, annotated to avoid gpu-node-2. watching pods come up.

jess: new replicas scheduling to node-3 and node-4, initial healthchecks passing. starting a rolling restart of the remaining pods on node-2 to free the GPU.

maria: customer impact: 12 requests failed with 5xx in last 2m. Affected customers: internal dashboard shows 3 customers with degraded throughput (low severity for now). No external outage page yet.

tyler.h: initiating a soft drain of gpu-node-2: kubectl cordon gpu-node-2 && drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -w

incident-bot: Action logged: node cordon + drain in progress (started 03:15:12).

jess: after restart of runtime on node-2 containers, memory usage dropped and no further OOM on restarted pods. Looks like a single process had leaked after a recent build.

maria: quick mitigation: revert recent runtime flag --prefetch-kv that landed in last deploy (2026-03-14 02:55). It increased persistent KV cache size.

tyler.h: rolling back config for model runtime on prod-serving to previous stable image: image: repo/runtime:2026-03-14-02-40 -> deploying

infra-bot: Rollout started for deployment/large-chat-v1.

jess: monitoring: error rate falling back to baseline. restarting alert suppression for this PagerDuty alert.

pagerduty: Incident update: Acknowledged and mitigation in flight. Escalation stopped.

tyler.h: handing off to jess for next shift monitoring — I need to jump to another page. jess, take over at 03:22.

jess: taking over oncall. I'll keep watch and follow up with post-incident notes. tagging infra for root-cause: @maria please capture memory profile and build diff.

maria: captured pprof and gpu memory trace from node-2, saved to s3://redwood-internal/incidents/INC12345/memory-profiles/. Diff shows --prefetch-kv flag increased KV prefetch window from 64->256 entries.

tyler.h: final status: mitigation applied, traffic routed away from affected node, rollback started. Will update incident ticket INC12345 with timeline.

jess: confirmed 30m after rollback that OOMs did not reoccur. Marking this as mitigated; continuing monitoring for 3 hours.

incident-bot: Incident INC12345 status: MITIGATED. PagerDuty alert auto-resolved at 03:44:10.

pagerduty: Note: follow-up action items: 1) revert or tune prefetch-kv default, 2) add guardrails to prevent single node saturation (autoscale downspill), 3) add better per-pod memory alerts (90th percentile across pods).

jess: creating postmortem draft and linking pprof and logs. Will include customer impact and timeline. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks — I'll prepare a small test to exercise prefetch window in staging to avoid regression.

tyler.h: great job team. closing thread once postmortem posted. :thumbsup:
